graphEvents.label: What must the output contract carry for a model to act on a command
Public schema has no kind and no runnable command field
Brief only says "use {label}" and never run or ask

label: The public recommendation object is a strict closed set of 13 fields; it has no kind and no runnable-command field, so either addition is a schema change, not a renderer tweak.

The only command-adjacent public field is optional workflowMode, which names a hub mode rather than a slash command, and the internal AdvisorRecommendation.kind is dropped at the boundary because it is optional and not in the schema.

The brief has exactly two sentence forms plus a fallback, and both operative forms say "use {label}" or "ambiguous: {label} … vs {label}", so the brief never instructs a run and never asks a question.
A non-doctor recommendation always renders as a skill label or raw id and the Also: companion line is doctor-only, so the brief has no syntax that can name a slash command for 28 of the 45 commands.
Declared budgets are 80 tokens normally, 120 when ambiguous, 120 maximum, at 4 characters per token.

The cap bounds only the routing head: the 13-character label plus 205-character hygiene directive are appended after the cap, so the emitted brief can reach about 134 tokens normally and 174 when ambiguous, above the stated 80 and the 120 maximum.

A typical normal brief measures 268 characters about 67 tokens, of which the actionable routing head is 50 characters about 13 tokens, so the routing payload is roughly a fifth of the brief and there is headroom for one command line without raising the cap.
The no-match fallback names no command except a hardcoded /doctor:setup hint that only fires for setup-shaped prompts, so a miss carries no route at all.
The model-facing contract asks for a SKILL ROUTING line built from the brief, so with a brief that can only say "use {label}" the model is structurally unable to report a command it was never told.

direction: Raising the brief token cap to fit command lines
reason: The routing head uses about 13 of 80 tokens; the cap overrun comes from a 218-character directive appended outside the cap
